newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends mid-range as dealers take profits.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends mid-range as dealers take profits.

text.p: IPE gas oil ended near the middle of a $4-range on Wednesday after a wave of profit-taking sliced into early gains prompted by a fall in U.S. distillate stocks and cold weather, brokers said.
Dec gas oil closed at $223.50 a tonne, up $2.00 from Tuesday but off a session high of $226.00. The January contract gained $3, trimming the prompt backwardation to $2.75 a tonne.
"The weather gave gas oil a lift but since then people have been taking profits in thin volume," said a broker.
The Energy Information Agency (EIA) said U.S. distillate stocks fell 900,000 barrels to 113.2 million last week.
Gas oil's early rally was helped by continued cold weather, brokers said.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp has said frigid weather should continue across the United States through the weekend.
"No one wants to be caught short (of heating oil)," said a broker.

Gas oil volumes were light, however, with several players waiting for the outcome of a duel between traders on the spot gas oil market involving the bulk of the record 865,100 tonnes due to be delivered between November 16-30 in Rotterdam.
Monte Carlo-based AIC, the main short on the expired November gas oil contract, plans to issue a statement about the delivery on Thursday.
IPE chief executive Lynton Jones said the exchange was monitoring the situation closely to ensure performance by both AIC and Swiss-based Cargill International SA, the dominant long.
Meanwhile, Jan Brent was also well off the session high of $23.70 after failing to fill a chart-gap to $23.77, brokers said.
At 1802 GMT, Jan Brent was trading up eight cents at $23.46 a barrel. -- Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
